description: Turns a MIDI transport's start, continue and stop signals into a reset pulse and a divided clock for a sequencer

inputs.text: A trigger above 2V sets the clock divisor count back to zero and starts the clock; the Reset output then pulses on the first frame the Clock input is high
A trigger above 2V starts the clock without clearing the divisor count and without a pulse at the Reset output
A trigger above 2V stops the clock; the Clock output drops to 0V
The clock being divided; each pulse above 2V is counted, and this jack's own voltage is what the Clock output passes on

outputs.text: Pulses once after a trigger at Start, carrying the Clock input's voltage for the single frame it appears; patch it to a sequencer's reset input
The Clock input passed on while the clock is running, thinned to one pulse in every group set by the Clock divisor menu

notes: the module comes up stopped and has no clock of its own; nothing appears at either output until a clock is patched to Clock and a trigger arrives at Start or Cont.
the note values printed in the Clock divisor menu assume the 96 pulses to a whole note that a MIDI clock sends, and the names ending in T are the triplet divisions.
patch the MIDI module's raw clock to the Clock input rather than a divided output, because the divisor menu does the dividing.
the green lamp near the top of the panel is lit while the clock is running.
